clue.text: Polish poet with single entry hard to follow

indicators.note: entry here means one letter making its way into the poet's name

parts.note: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet
single is one, the Roman numeral I
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Polish poet is told that a solo entrance will be difficult to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb. 'entry' puts I inside BURNS; 'to follow' sets H after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To burnish metal is to rub it until it shines, a synonym of polish.

clue.text: Paid for fare and got into train

definitions.meaning: took meals and lodging in return for payment

explanation.definitionFit: A lodger who boarded paid for food, and a passenger who boarded climbed aboard.

clue.text: Check condition and put back in place

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
state means condition

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the condition of a thing and puts it back.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore something or someone to a former position.

clue.text: Individual not to open fire

indicators.note: not to open means the first letter of the word for individual is dropped

parts.note: single means individual, one only

explanation.surface: Someone is told individually not to light the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fire on a domestic hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Uncertainty shown by fellow I met in Scottish station

parts.note: HE, a male person, a fellow

indicators.note: met in means the first-person letter is encountered inside the station word

parts.note: in Scotland a stance is a stand or site, such as a taxi rank or bus station

explanation.surface: A man's hesitation when he bumps into the speaker at a Scottish station.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the 'I' that the page prints after 'fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitance is hesitation, a state of doubt or indecision.

clue.text: Calm current in South American river

indicators.note: in places the electrical term inside the name of the river

parts.note: the River Plate, the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A calm current flows in a South American river.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to soothe or pacify them, a synonym of calm as a verb.

clue.text: Religious leader who's said to conduct Inquisition?

indicators.note: said signals that the word for an inquisitive person is heard, not seen

parts.note: one who conducts an inquisition pries, so is a pryer

explanation.surface: A churchman is rumoured to have run the Inquisition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inquisition' points to the Spanish Inquisition, but simply means prying.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior is the head of a priory, a monastic house.

clue.text: Gave up as mounted police declined to go outside

indicators.note: to go outside means the word for declined wraps round the police letters

parts.note: abated means declined or lessened

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means climbing, so the police letters read upward

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Mounted police refused to go out, and gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted police' paints officers on horseback, but in a down clue 'mounted' means the police letters climb, reading upward; 'to go outside' wraps the word for declined round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or responsibility.

clue.text: Showing a strong passion

parts.note: a person consumed by ardour is figuratively burning with it, lit up by feeling

explanation.definitionFit: To be on fire with emotion is to be ardent, burning with feeling.

clue.text: Fully occupy rude quarters at the top

indicators.note: in a down clue at the top puts the quarters above the rude word

parts.note: E and N are compass points, quarters of the compass
gross means coarse or rude

explanation.surface: Vulgar living quarters on the top floor take up all one's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross someone is to absorb all their attention.

clue.text: Presenting imitation brooch in silver case

indicators.note: the silver forms a case around the brooch, enclosing it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a brooch is a pin fastened to clothing

explanation.surface: A jeweller shows a copy of a brooch set in a silver case.
explanation.definitionFit: Aping someone means mimicking them, so it presents an imitation.

clue.text: Twisting and turning across lake on skis, initially

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word skis
across means the turning stretches either side of the lake abbreviation

parts.note: winding means turning, as a road does
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A skier twists and turns across a lake, starting on skis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S from skis, which leads the answer though it ends the clue; 'across' puts L inside WINDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindling is cheating someone, and twisting is slang for cheating or defrauding.

clue.text: He won't go along with trip for residents

indicators.note: a trip for these letters is a tumble that rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to join the residents on their outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip for' is the anagram signal: RESIDENTS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter is someone who disagrees with the majority view and refuses to conform.

clue.text: Firm split by revolutionary belief

indicators.note: split by means the company abbreviation is broken open with the colour word inside it

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a red is a communist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: A company is divided by a radical over its creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of what one believes, a creed.

clue.text: Exhaust pipe

definitions.meaning: to exhaust is to use up or deplete completely
a pipe carrying away waste water or sewage

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means deplete, as in tiring someone out; as a noun it is a channel for waste water.

clue.text: Dangerously close encounter with new world in dawn of galaxy

parts.note: Earth, the world

indicators.note: dawn of means the beginning, the opening letter of galaxy

explanation.surface: A near collision with a newly found planet at the edge of a galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape, a situation where disaster was only just avoided.

clue.text: Minimal changes in sea levels despite an upheaval

indicators.note: an upheaval throws the words despite and an into disorder, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Sea levels barely change despite some geological upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the tides of least range, occurring at the moon's first and third quarters.

clue.text: Recorder of rise and fall of Hercules, perhaps

definitions.text: Recorder of rise and fall of Hercules, perhaps

parts.words: Recorder of rise and fall of Hercules, perhaps
parts.note: reads like a chronicler of the hero's fortunes, but Hercules is the Lockheed transport aircraft and the rise and fall is its height

explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures height above sea level, as in an aircraft cockpit.

clue.text: Tyranny of Paris initially evident in fashion of modistes

indicators.note: evident in means the opening letter shows up inside the rearranged dressmakers
to fashion is to shape, so the dressmakers' letters are remade
initially takes the first letter of Paris

explanation.surface: The dictatorship of Paris shows in the dressmakers' styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion of' rearranges MODISTES (dressmakers) into DESOTISM, and 'evident in' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotism is rule by an absolute ruler, a form of tyranny.

clue.text: A learner taken in to Stay, as usual

indicators.note: taken in to means the article and the learner abbreviation are placed inside the word for stay

parts.note: to stay something is to stop or prevent it, as in staying an execution
L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver is invited to stay, as is customary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like an invitation but means halt, PREVENT, with AL put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread or commonly found, hence usual.

clue.text: Standard surmounting a favourite defensive work

indicators.note: in a down clue surmounting puts the standard on top of what follows

parts.note: par is the standard, as in golf
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A flag flies above a favourite fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests a flag, a picture the surface supports, but means PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along a rampart or roof.

clue.text: One's note gaining admission to party in dance centre

indicators.note: the first pieces are let into the word for party, going inside it

parts.note: a do is a party
one is I, so one's is I'S
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone's banknote gets them into a party at a dance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club or venue where people dance to recorded music.

clue.text: After bowling spell, spinner gets cap

indicators.note: after places the spinning toy behind the cricket term

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: After a spell of bowling, a spin bowler wins an international cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' and 'cap' suggest cricket, but the spinner is a toy and cap a verb meaning outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or surpass, as to cap something is to outdo it.

clue.text: Criticise cook

definitions.meaning: to ... meat is to cook it in an oven

explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for harsh criticism and also the oven method for meat.

clue.text: In the main, somewhat perplexed

definitions.meaning: the main is the open sea, so in the main means out on the ocean
confused, not knowing what to do

explanation.definitionFit: Literally out on the ocean, and figuratively bewildered or lost.

clue.text: Fruit flavour used in making rock

parts.note: limes are citrus fruit
flavour can mean the distinctive quality or character of something, its tone

explanation.surface: A lime flavouring goes into making a stick of seaside rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests the seaside sweet, but it is the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sedimentary rock made largely of calcium carbonate.

clue.text: Windblown soil deprivation besetting East

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the deprivation word encloses the compass point

parts.note: loss is deprivation

explanation.surface: Wind erosion leaves the eastern soil impoverished.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine yellowish sediment deposited by the wind.

clue.text: Steps taken by Weller to some degree

parts.note: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: Weller takes steps to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: A samba is a Brazilian dance, and a dance is a sequence of steps.

clue.text: Vexing when held in check on both sides of crossing place

indicators.note: the confined word is split so its letters stand either side of the crossing place

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means held in or confined
a stile is a set of steps for crossing a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Something is annoying because it is restrained either side of a crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent, besides meaning plague-bearing, can mean annoying or troublesome.

clue.text: Damp fog — nothing discernible in it

indicators.note: something discernible in it can be seen within the fog, so the zero sits inside

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A damp fog in which nothing can be made out.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, a synonym of damp.

clue.text: It may irritate viewers when broadcast

definitions.text: It may irritate viewers when broadcast

parts.words: It may irritate viewers when broadcast
parts.note: reads like a complaint about a television programme, but the viewers are eyes and broadcast means scattered through the air

explanation.definitionFit: This chemical agent is sprayed to disperse crowds by making their eyes stream.

clue.text: Indicator of turnings in mine passage leading to face

indicators.note: leading to puts the passage word before the face word

parts.note: in mining, a road is an underground passage
map is slang for face

explanation.surface: Miners find their way along a passage that leads to the coalface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' suggests the coalface, but MAP is slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A road map shows the routes and junctions where one must turn.
